correctness.rationale: The endpoints of the single deleted edge are the only pair at distance three; same-shore pairs have a common neighbor and every other cross-shore pair is adjacent. Thus the only forbidden triples consist of one star edge from each missing-edge endpoint and their unique joining interior edge. For star index sets A,B all ab edges in B times A are unavailable and the other rs-ab are freely selectable. A facet must fill every permitted interior position. If both stars contribute, a missing star edge would then close a triple with any selected edge on the opposite star, proving sufficiency; if exactly one star contributes, it must be complete, giving the two exceptional facets; both empty cannot be maximal. For a,b>=1, a+b-ab=1-(a-1)(b-1)<=1, attained if either index count is one. The exceptional sizes rs+r and rs+s therefore determine the maximum and its one/two-fold multiplicity, and comparison to mn gives the claimed loss. When r=s=k>=3 the two attained sizes k^2+1 and k^2+k flank the claimed gap.
residual_risks: The replay independently derives geodesics by BFS and exhausts all subsets and one-edge extensions in six small instances up to (5,5), reproducing 3839105 eligible sets and 227 facets there. It does not replace the proof for arbitrary shore sizes. The frozen C++ reproducer uses a GNU header and builtin (works under the specified g++ rather than being strictly portable ISO-only C++17).

value.rationale: A single deletion creates the first geodesic constraints in a previously unconstrained graph. The full facet classification quantifies the disruption: many inclusion-maximal sets, a precise optimum drop, and a growing gap just below the maximum in the balanced case. This is a natural exact invariant and a sharp baseline for further matching deletions, not merely a scalar calculation on a small graph.
residual_risks: The result is specific to a single missing edge and does not classify further deletions.
